title: Cost per recording channel
contract: Nominal hardware purchase price divided by simultaneously acquired electrical recording channels in the priced configuration.

records.name: NeuroRighter
records.dateBasis: Plotted by paper publication year (2009). Component prices are October 2008 except recording headstages, November 2007.
records.included: Recording headstages and cables, filtering and power boards, A/D cards, breakout boxes, circuit components, and a computer.
records.excluded: Monitor (explicit Table 4 footnote), electrodes, and implantation.
records.channelBasis: 64 simultaneously acquired broadband inputs at 25 kHz/channel, 16-bit. Spike and LFP bands are not counted twice.
records.caveat: The prose says “with monitor,” but Table 4 explicitly says no monitor. This mock uses the itemized table boundary, not the conflicting prose.

evidence.label: Price date · table footnote
evidence.text: Prices as of October 2008, except for recording headstages: November 2007.

evidence.label: Recording denominator
evidence.text: Our system has 16-bit resolution, and has been used in practice for 64 channels of simultaneous spike and LFP acquisition.

records.name: Open Ephys
records.dateBasis: Plotted by paper publication year (2017). This is a published purchase-price bound, not a dated itemized vendor quote.
records.included: A 64-channel Open Ephys system as described by the authors; the cost passage does not itemize its components.
records.excluded: Computer and electrode inclusion are not specified in the price passage. No implantation cost is established.
records.channelBasis: 64 is the priced configuration. The platform’s maximum of 512 simultaneous channels is not the denominator for this price.
records.caveat: Less than stays less than. The downward arrow means the actual ratio is below the plotted ceiling; it is not an error bar or an exact price.

evidence.label: Price + priced denominator
evidence.text: a 64-channel Open Ephys system can be purchased for less than $3000

evidence.label: Capacity is not the priced denominator
evidence.text: If eight 64-channel chips are used, a total of 512 channels can be recorded simultaneously.

records.name: Science SciFi 2
records.dateBasis: Plotted by public price observation year (2026), not product launch or a historical SciFi price.
records.included: One SciFi 2 headstage + one Neuropixels 1.0 adapter. Academic: $2,130 + $532. List: $8,454 + $2,130.
records.excluded: Probe, computer, accessories, tax, shipping, surgery, and labor.
records.channelBasis: 384 simultaneous recording channels through the priced adapter. AP and LFP from the same inputs are not additional channels.
records.caveat: A derived sum of two public part prices, not a turnkey quote. Academic and commercial list prices must remain visibly separate.

evidence.label: Recording denominator
evidence.text: Up to 384 channels of dual band neural recording (AP and LFP bands) from 960 recording sites

records.name: Science SciFi 2
records.dateBasis: Plotted by public price observation year (2026), not product launch or a historical SciFi price.
records.included: One SciFi 2 headstage + one Cereport adapter. Academic: $2,130 + $532. List: $8,454 + $2,130.
records.excluded: Probe, computer, accessories, tax, shipping, surgery, and labor. Utah array and pedestal are not included.
records.channelBasis: 96 simultaneous recording channels through the priced adapter. The 128 connector pins are not 128 recording channels.
records.caveat: A derived sum of two public part prices, not a turnkey quote. Academic and commercial list prices must remain visibly separate.

evidence.label: Recording denominator
evidence.text: There are 96 broadband channels available from the 128 pin pedestal, following the typical electrode layout of the 96 channel Utah Array.

records.name: Open Ephys
records.dateBasis: Plotted by current variant-price observation year (2026), not the 2017 paper price.
records.included: Acquisition board, power supply, USB cable, two 64-channel unipolar headstages, two SPI tethers, two I/O boards, and two HDMI cables.
records.channelBasis: Two supplied headstages × 64 unipolar channels = 128. Not the 512-channel maximum and not the lower-priced 2 × 16-channel bipolar bundle.
records.caveat: The headline “from” price belongs to a different configuration. This row uses the exact OEPS-9113 / No Training variant.

evidence.label: Variant · exact API fields
evidence.text: Training: "No Training"; Headstages: "[OEPS-6570] Low-profile SPI Headstage 64ch (Hirose)"

records.name: Blackrock Utah array
records.dateBasis: Plotted by original article publication year (2016). The approximate price is contemporary journalism, not an original vendor quotation.
records.included: Electrode array only, as reported by The Salt Lake Tribune.
records.excluded: Other necessary equipment. Exact SKU and connector/pedestal inclusion are unspecified; no complete recording setup is priced.
records.channelBasis: 96 active recording channels in the same article’s photo caption. The body’s 100 physical needles are not the recording denominator.
records.caveat: An approximate, weaker historical checkpoint. Do not present it as an exact manufacturer quote or a full-system baseline.

evidence.label: Approximate array price
evidence.text: The array costs about $6,000, not including other necessary equipment.

evidence.label: Recording denominator · photo caption
evidence.text: The company has developed the Utah Array, an implantable 96-channel microelectrode that is helping a man paralyzed from the shoulders down restore movement in his hand.

records.name: Neuropixels 2.0
records.dateBasis: Plotted by observation year (2026) of the undated official RFQ v9.3.0, not the probe’s release year.
records.included: A box of five single-shank probes. €7,500 ÷ 5 = €1,500 allocated per probe; minimum priced purchase is the full €7,500 box.
records.excluded: Headstage, cable, acquisition hardware, and surgery. Research use only in nonhuman subjects. No single-unit €1,500 offer is verified.
records.channelBasis: 384 parallel full-band recording channels per probe, 30 kHz, 12-bit. The 1,280 selectable sites are not all simultaneous channels.
records.caveat: A per-probe allocation of a box price, not a standalone offer or a complete setup. Do not combine this NP 2.0 price with the NP 1.0 adapter row.

evidence.text: NP2003 | Box of 5 Neuropixels 2.0 single shank probes | 7,500

evidence.text: NP2004 | Box of 5 Neuropixels 2.0 single shank probes with cap | 7,500

evidence.text: 384 parallel, full-band (AP, LFP), low-noise recording channels
